description: Club members, one per row (240 rows): member_id (whole number), full_name (first and last name; many names have accented letters; capital letters and spaces around the name are inconsistent), home_city (city name, several with accented letters; capital letters and spaces around the name are inconsistent; about 3% of cells are empty and about 3% hold "-" for an unknown city), fee (yearly fee, two decimals).

Weekly sales per shop branch (180 rows): branch_code (five-digit branch code written with leading zeros, e.g. "01005"; 12 different branches, each appearing in many rows), week (week number 1-15), sales (units sold, whole number; about 3% of cells are empty).

Shop price list (64 rows): sku (text code such as "PL-0007"), item (product name with size; several names have accented letters), section (dairy, pantry, drinks or bakery; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), price (written with exactly two decimals, e.g. "9.50"; no empty cells).

Account sign-ups (300 rows, not in date order): account_id (whole number), signup_day (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD, between 2023 and 2025; no empty cells), channel (web, app, referral or partner; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent; about 2% empty), first_payment (amount with two decimals; about 5% empty).

Shipments (400 rows): shipment_id (whole number), ordered_on and shipped_on (dates as text, YYYY-MM-DD, in 2025; shipped_on is empty for about 4% of rows that have not shipped yet), carrier (DHL, UPS, PostNord or GLS; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), weight_kg (one decimal), value (order value, two decimals).

Website clicks (500 rows): click_ref (seven-digit reference with leading zeros, e.g. "0000011"), epoch_s (Unix timestamp in seconds, UTC, whole number), epoch_ms (Unix timestamp in milliseconds, UTC, when the click was received, whole number), page (site path such as /home or /pricing), dwell_s (seconds on the page, one decimal; about 8% empty).

Clinic appointments in New York (160 rows, February to November 2025, so the clock changes in March and November fall inside the data): appt_id (whole number), local_start (New York wall-clock start, text YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, no UTC offset), start_with_offset (the same moment as ISO text with its UTC offset, e.g. "2025-06-13T08:45:00-04:00"), clinic (Harbor, Midtown or Riverside; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty).

Company revenue per calendar quarter (30 rows, oldest first, one row per quarter with no gaps): quarter_start (first day of the quarter as text, YYYY-MM-DD, from 2019-01-01 to 2026-04-01), revenue (whole number), new_accounts (whole number).

Website sessions in June 2025 (250 rows, not in time order): session_id (whole number), user_code (five-digit code with leading zeros), started_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS; no empty cells), pages_viewed (whole number; about 3% empty), device (desktop, mobile or tablet; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent).

Hotel bookings (300 rows): booking_id (whole number), state (paid, cancelled, refunded or pending; mostly lower case, some with other capitals or extra spaces), total (booking amount, two decimals; refunded bookings are negative), nights (whole number; about 2% empty).

Hospital admissions (260 rows): admission_id (whole number), age (years, whole number; about 5% empty), ward (cardiology, oncology, maternity, orthopedics or neurology; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), stay_days (whole number; about 3% empty), charge (two decimals; about 5% empty).

Water gauge log (120 rows): gauge (gauge name such as "LA-01"), reading (meters, three decimals; about 3% empty), level (alert level, whole number from 3 to 80, no empty cells), site (dam, canal or lake; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent).

Streaming subscribers, one per row (320 rows): subscriber_id (whole number), age (years, from 19 to 87; about 1% empty), tier (basic, plus or premium; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), monthly_fee (two decimals; about 3% empty), joined_year (whole number).

Shop purchases (900 rows): purchase_id (whole number), subscriber_id (refers to subscribers.csv; most subscribers have several purchases), store_city (city name; the same city is written with different capitals and extra spaces, e.g. "lisbon" and "LISBON"; about 2% empty), quantity (whole number), spend (two decimals).

Weekly unit sales (144 rows): region (north, south or west), channel (online, store or kiosk; the west region has no kiosk, so that pair never occurs), week (week number 1-18), units (whole number; about 2% empty).

Daily visitor counts at the north entrance (36 rows, rows not in date order, each day at most once, some days missing): day (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD, September-October 2025), visitors (whole number; equal counts are common), remark (short note; about 47% empty). The dates overlap only partly with footfall_south.csv.

Daily visitor counts at the south entrance (36 rows, rows not in date order, each day at most once, some days missing): day (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD, September-October 2025), visitors (whole number; equal counts are common), remark (short note; about 47% empty). The dates overlap only partly with footfall_north.csv.

Loyalty memberships (200 rows): member_ref (six-digit reference with leading zeros), plan (bronze, silver, gold or platinum), city (city name; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent in some rows), points (whole number, multiples of 50; many members share the same points).

Exam scores (60 rows, one per student): student (full name, unique, many with accented letters), then math, art and music (scores 35-100, whole numbers; about 9% of these score cells are empty, and one student has no score at all).
Product returns in March (80 rows): return_id (whole number), quantity (whole number), refund (two decimals). Same columns as returns_april.csv.
Product returns in April: the header row (return_id, quantity, refund, as in returns_march.csv) and no data rows, because nothing was returned in April.

Parcel deliveries (240 rows): delivery_id (whole number), city (city name; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), status (exactly "shipped" or "pending", always lower case, no empty cells), parcels (whole number; about 2% empty), express (True or False; about 5% empty).

Daily store traffic (90 rows): store (name such as "Store 07"), sales (whole number of sales, zero on some days), visits (whole number of visits, zero on some days; about 3% empty), open_sunday (True or False; about 8% empty).
Quiz results (80 rows, one per student in seat order, no other columns): quiz_a and quiz_b (points 0-10, whole numbers, many equal values; about 9% and 6% of cells empty for absent students).

Order lines (300 rows): line_id (whole number), product (product name; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), quantity (whole number; about 3% empty), amount (line total, two decimals; about 3% empty).
Product code changes (150 rows): product (name with model), stock_qty (whole number), old_code and new_code (four-digit whole numbers; the code is unchanged in 100 rows). No empty cells.
Parcel price table (120 rows, sorted by weight_kg, each weight once): weight_kg (two decimals, from 0.40 to 54.05, never a whole number), zones (whole number 1-5), fee (two decimals; about 4% empty).

Cloud storage accounts (150 rows): account_id (whole number), active (True or False), quota_bytes (storage limit in bytes, whole number; the 23 unlimited accounts carry the value 9223372036854775807), used_bytes (whole number). No empty cells.

Daily weather at one station (90 rows, one per day in date order from 2025-06-01, no gaps): date (YYYY-MM-DD), temp_c (mean temperature in degrees C, two decimals; about 1% empty), humidity (percent, whole number).

Tasting competition scores (96 rows): panel (one of 8 panels, e.g. bread or cheese; 12 entrants each), entrant (person name; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), score (4.0-10.0, one decimal; no empty cells).

Bike-share riders, one per row (400 rows): rider_id (six-digit id with leading zeros), display_name (person name, some with accented letters), home_district (one of 6 districts such as "Old Town"), membership (casual, monthly or annual) - these three text columns have inconsistent capital letters and stray spaces; joined_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD; about 2% empty), birth_year (whole number; about 4% empty), credit_balance (two decimals, can be negative; about 5% empty).

Bike-share stations (48 rows, one per station): station_code (four-digit code with leading zeros, e.g. "0040"), station_name (text, a few with accented letters), district (same 6 districts as riders.csv; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), docks (whole number), opened_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD).

Bike-share trips, 1 September to 1 November 2025 (1500 rows): trip_id (whole number), rider_id (refers to riders.csv), start_station and end_station (refer to station_code in stations.csv), started_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty), distance_km (two decimals), fare (two decimals; about 3% empty), payment (card, app or cash; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), rating (1-5 stars, whole number; about 19% empty).

Hourly weather for the city, September 2025 (720 rows, one per hour in time order, no gaps): observed_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), temp_c (degrees C, one decimal; about 2% empty), rain_mm (one decimal), wind_kmh (whole number), sky (clear, cloudy, fog or rain; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent).

Planned fare changes (30 rows, one per affected station): station_code (refers to stations.csv; four digits with leading zeros), effective_from (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD), new_base_fare (two decimals; about 3% empty).
